title: Quiz: Setting Up the R Modelling Environment

questions.text: Which chunk option suppresses package loading messages without hiding the code?
questions.explanation: message = FALSE suppresses informational messages (like those printed when loading tidyverse) while still showing the code (echo = TRUE by default) and still running it. include = FALSE hides both code and output; eval = FALSE shows code but does not run it.

questions.text: You should put install.packages() inside a chunk with eval = TRUE so the packages are reinstalled each time you knit.
questions.explanation: install.packages() should be in a chunk with eval = FALSE. It only needs to run once per machine. Reinstalling on every knit wastes time and can break reproducibility if package versions change.

questions.text: What does diamonds |> filter(carat > 1) |> summarise(m = mean(price)) compute?
options: The mean price of all diamonds
The mean price of diamonds weighing more than 1 carat
The number of diamonds with carat > 1
The median carat among expensive diamonds
questions.explanation: The pipe chains operations left to right: start with diamonds, keep only rows where carat > 1, then compute the mean of price. The result is a single number — the mean price among heavy diamonds.

questions.text: In the diamonds dataset, the mean price ($3,933) is higher than the median price ($2,401). What does this tell you about the price distribution?
options: Price is left-skewed — most diamonds are expensive
Price is right-skewed — a small number of very expensive diamonds pull the mean up
The mean and median should always be equal
questions.explanation: When mean > median, the distribution is right-skewed. There are many affordable diamonds and a small tail of very expensive ones. Those high-priced outliers pull the mean above the median, but the median is unaffected — it only depends on rank order.

questions.text: You run ggplot(diamonds, aes(carat, price, colour = cut)) + geom_smooth(method = 'lm', se = FALSE). How many fitted lines appear?
options: One line for the entire dataset
One line per row of diamonds
One line per cut level (5 lines total)
questions.explanation: When colour = cut is mapped, geom_smooth() fits a separate model within each group defined by cut. Since cut has 5 levels (Fair, Good, Very Good, Premium, Ideal), five lines appear, one per level.

questions.text: In the diamonds dataset, 'Ideal' cut diamonds always have a higher mean price than 'Fair' cut diamonds, even before controlling for carat.
questions.explanation: Counterintuitively, 'Fair' cut diamonds have a higher raw mean price than 'Ideal' diamonds. This is because cut is confounded with carat size: lower-quality cuts are applied to larger rough stones, so they are heavier and more expensive on raw price. Only after controlling for carat in a regression model does the quality premium for Ideal cuts become visible.
